data.why: The app has no file upload widget for netCDF data; the scientist types a filesystem path into a sidebar text field, defaulting to data/sample/sample_atmos.nc, which the bundled scripts/make_sample_data.py (run as part of the start command, as the README's Usage section shows) generates with realistic 4-D (time, level, lat, lon) atmospheric fields (t, z, u, v), 3-D precip, and 3-D sst with high-latitude NaNs.

goals: Load a netCDF dataset and inspect its variables, coordinates and detected lat/lon/vertical/time roles
Build a horizontal map of a field on a given level and time with a chosen map projection and contour/vector layers
Build a vertical or time cross-section of a 4-D field along a chosen path or location
Make a 1-D line plot or distribution (histogram/ECDF/box/violin) of a variable along a non-spatial dimension
Export the finished figure as PNG/SVG/PDF and also export a standalone reproduction script (xarray/matplotlib/cartopy)
Save and reload a session (JSON) capturing the full figure configuration for later reuse

review.summary: The tree describes ClimCanvas's purpose and its load, plot and export workflow well, with faithful labels, well-cut features and screens that match every node I checked. But the headline map never rendered, and the tree falsely reports the distribution and 2-D aggregate modes as missing (they sit lower in the Plot mode list), so it needs a supplementary run before it is filed.
